faq.a: It means choosing to let go of anger about what they did, so it stops weighing you down. It does not mean the hurt was okay, or that you must forget.
asks: Tell me about the Tunde decides

faq.q: Is it okay to still feel angry?
faq.a: Yes. Forgiving can take time, and feelings can come back. Talking, breathing and giving it time all help.

faq.q: Do I have to forgive someone who keeps hurting me?
faq.a: Forgiving is your choice. If someone hurts you again and again, you can forgive in your heart and still keep away from them. Always tell a trusted adult.
asks: Do I have to be friends again after I forgive?

faq.q: Why is forgiving good for me?
faq.a: Holding on to anger can make you feel tense and unhappy. Letting go helps you feel lighter and calmer.
Notice your hurt, talk about it, think about why they might have done it, and decide to let go. It is fine if it takes a few tries.

facts: Many psychologists define forgiveness as letting go of resentment, which is different from forgetting or excusing what happened.
Research has linked forgiving with lower stress and better wellbeing.
